summary: Iteration 50 — validated the new comment REPLY feature (creator quote-reply), admin delete of comment/reply, anti-spam ignoring is_reply, push broadcasts on ad + marketplace approval. 13/13 pytest cases pass against the public preview URL. Frontend code review confirms all data-testid attributes and logic (isCreator / canReply / canDelete / quoteBlock / replyPreview) are correctly implemented in ads.tsx. However, live browser verification of the reply/delete UI could not be completed — while the ads feed and comments render, the per-comment inner View testIDs (ad-comment-item-*) are not surfaced in the DOM by react-native-web 0.21 and the Reply/Delete icons never appeared, most likely because the useAuth user context resolves as null in that render path (see details).

ui_bugs.issue: Reply and Delete icons never render next to comments even when logged in as admin (who is BOTH the creator of the seeded ad AND role=admin). Root cause hypothesis: the `user` object from useAuth() is null/undefined inside renderAd() — my fetch to /api/auth/me using localStorage.auth_token returned 401 'Token invalide', so the client-side session is likely being restored from a different place (react-native-async-storage token, refresh cookie) OR expired. In either case, `user?.id === item.user_id` and `user?.role === 'admin'` evaluate false and the two TouchableOpacity blocks (data-testid ad-comment-reply-{id} / ad-comment-delete-{id}) are skipped.

The outer <View testID={`ad-comment-item-${c.id}`}> does NOT surface a data-testid attribute on the DOM element (verified via full document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid]') dump — 35 total testids, zero matching ad-comment-item-*). Same for ad-comment-quote-{id}. Comments text still renders correctly, only the testID is missing. Likely a react-native-web 0.21 quirk when a View has only Text children and no interactive props — testID gets dropped. Suggest adding accessibilityLabel or an onLayout/onPress no-op to force RN-Web to keep testID, OR use nativeID as a fallback.

action_items: Investigate why useAuth().user is null inside AdsScreenInner even when the ads feed loads (looks like session restore path — auth_token in localStorage returns 401 against /api/auth/me but the api client still gets ads. Check src/auth.tsx / src/api.ts token source and refresh flow, and ensure the SAME token used for /ads works for /auth/me).

Add fallback so per-comment View DOM node keeps its testID under react-native-web 0.21. Two options: (a) pass an accessibilityLabel or nativeID={`ad-comment-item-${c.id}`} on the View, (b) upgrade RN-web, or (c) wrap the View in a Pressable with no-op onPress (Pressable always surfaces data-testid on web).
Same fix needed for ad-comment-quote-{id} View (line 284 of ads.tsx).

rca of the issue: Backend RCA: none (all endpoints pass). Frontend RCA (hypothesis): the Reply/Delete icons are conditionally rendered on `user?.id === item.user_id` and `user?.role === 'admin'`. In our browser session useAuth().user is likely null at render time — a fetch to /api/auth/me with the localStorage.auth_token yields 401 while the same session successfully loads /api/ads via the api client. This mismatch strongly suggests the api client is using an in-memory / refreshed token that has NOT been persisted (or the persisted token is stale). Verify src/auth.tsx bootstraps `user` from /api/auth/me on mount — if that call 401s, user stays null forever and the whole conditional UI disappears. Fix path: (1) ensure the fresh token from login is what api.ts uses AND what /auth/me is called with; (2) if 401, force a refresh or logout instead of silently staying with user=null.
